report:
**Conclusion: the claim is true in the United States, not false.** Kyleena (19.5-mg levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) is FDA-approved to prevent pregnancy **for up to five years**. The FDA-approved label says it must be removed by the end of year 5; a new Kyleena may be inserted at removal if contraception is still wanted.

The duration is supported by a clinical study of 1,452 generally healthy participants aged 18–35, including people who had and had not previously given birth. In that study, the first-year Pearl Index was 0.16 (about 0.16 pregnancies per 100 users in one year); 13 pregnancies produced an estimated cumulative five-year pregnancy rate of 1.45% (upper 95% confidence limit 2.53%). Thus, “up to five years” is an approved use backed by five-year trial follow-up—not a guarantee that pregnancy is impossible.

An understandable source of confusion is that other levonorgestrel IUDs have different approved durations (and may contain different hormone amounts). Those durations should not be applied interchangeably to Kyleena. Evidence retrieved does **not** support the view that the stated five-year approval is false. It also does not establish reliable use *beyond* five years; replacement/removal at five years remains the labeled instruction.
